status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Where feasible and useful, AI actors should provide plain explanations of relevant inputs, factors, processes or logic so affected people can understand AI outputs.
review.reason_for_change: The parent is affected by a generated-image refusal and needs a meaningful explanation of the relevant input/factors, directly engaging the OECD plain-explanation proposition where useful. The screenshot supplies guardrail categories and retry guidance, but hides the eight detailed image instructions and the generated image. It cannot resolve whether that explanation accurately identifies the operative factors or whether further disclosure was feasible. A benign visible prompt prefix alone does not establish an inaccurate explanation.

conclusion_change.previous: The visible user purpose is an ordinary children’s drawing lesson, while the displayed refusal invokes a serious content category in relation to an unseen generated image. That mismatch warrants scrutiny, but the omitted eight-image instructions and unseen image prevent a finding that the refusal reason was unsupported or the safety control activated invalidly. The author’s claim of prompt rewriting is not accompanied by a before-and-after trace. VIGIL records the concrete refusal and an explanation/provenance boundary without converting the incomplete screenshot into a class-level diagnosis. Both clauses retain unresolved status: an unseen generated image may explain the refusal category, and no compared prompt versions demonstrate lineage distortion. The evidence supports neither a refusal-explanation failure nor a successful safeguard finding. No eligible candidate is derived from these unresolved relationships, and no independently source-identified admitted requirement is established. The whole occurrence remains partially adjudicated without an external finding.
